This Camper Van Was Built by a Master Welder and It's Reinforced From the Frame Up
21 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy
Lots of skills are transferable to camper van building. The most popular one is woodworking, but there are others, like welding, that can make a difference in how well you can build a home on wheels. That's the case with the van I'd like to discuss today and the man behind the conversion.
What we have here is a project based on an AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170" wheelbase. It was created by Cody through his Redmond, Oregon-based company, Untrapped Solutions . I dig the name, it's fitting considering what the company does.
Cody is a master welder and craftsman, having worked as a welder at a ski resort, fabricating rails and boxes without exposed fasteners to help keep riders safe. Moreover, in 2016, he converted his first van and founded Untrapped Solutions in 2020 out of a deep love for the outdoors and travel.
As always, let's first take a look at the exterior. For starters, the van rides on Method wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich KO3 all-terrain tires. Cody further upgraded the van's off-road capabilities by installing an Agile Offroad RIP suspension kit, which comes with front coilovers, rear Fox shocks, and custom-rate rear leaf spring packs.
You can use a ladder on the driver's side to climb on top of the van. There, you'll discover a Roambuilt roof rack that holds a flat-mounted Starlink antenna, a Fiamma F45S awning, and a huge deck platform where you can chill and enjoy the surrounding views. What's more, two cut-outs make space for a Maxxair vent fan and an A/C unit.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy At the rear, you'll come across an Agile Offroad spare tire carrier and an Aluminess PowerLift motorized bike rack. Other notable mods are Roambuilt side steps, and power and water hookups.
The interior is the most distinctive part of the build. Cody does a few things differently in his projects. For instance, all the cabinetry is built around a tubular steel frame that's not fully enclosed in the wood – the frames are the cornerstone of the cabinetry.
This construction makes for a very durable and sturdy setup. Furthermore, Untrapped Solutions takes pride in reinforcing the "bones" of the van itself by installing aluminum reinforcements throughout the van.
You'll notice that the interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. What's more, the passenger seat is mounted on a swivel base, so it can be turned around to face the back of the van.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy This van's customer is an architect, and she has an eye for design. She opted for a welcoming, colorful aesthetic – it consists of beige Lonseal Lonridge flooring, a mix of bamboo and blue laminated cabinetry with black framing, walls upholstered in grey woven fabric, and a faux leather ceiling.
The look is complemented by a white solid surface countertop, a bamboo trim for the bathroom door, and pops of color, like an orange panel in the seating area.
Straight ahead of the entrance, Cody devised a bathroom. It has a shower with a handheld sprayer, a white Laveo dry-flush toilet, an L-Track on the back wall for hanging stuff, and a retractable Nautilus door that prevents water from splashing outside the bathroom.
Next, we have the kitchen that's split into two parts, one on each side of the living space. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a pull-out faucet, a single-burner induction stovetop, and an Isotherm fridge with a tiny freezer compartment. On its outer panel that faces the entrance, it has a flip-down table supported by small gas struts.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy Walk just a bit deeper inside the van and you'll reach the dinette area. It comprises two benches facing one another, with a decently sized Lagun table in between.
You can turn the dinette into a small bed, and it's quite simple and quick to do. You must remove the tabletop and use it alongside an extra panel to connect the two benches. Then, rearrange the cushions, and you're good to go. The result is a bed that's 72 inches (182 centimeters) long.
Finally, the rear part of the living space is taken up by a fixed sleeping arrangement measuring 76 inches (193 centimeters) in length and 67 inches (170 centimeters) in width. It offers four overhead cabinets (two on each side), an iPad mount, and two reading lights next to the rear doors. Above, a Nomadic Cooling A/C unit will keep you cool when needed.
The go-to storage spot for gear and bulky items is the garage underneath the bedroom, which is accessible only from the back of the van, after opening the rear doors. It offers abundant storage space in the middle and also has two massive boxes on the sides that accommodate the utility systems.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are an 800 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. You can top off the batteries by using three sources: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 33-gallon (125-liter) freshwater tank, two under-mounted greywater tanks, and an outdoor shower connection with a mixer. Furthermore, a Rixen's hydronic heating system provides both heated air and hot water.
All in all, every detail in this camper van by Cody and Untrapped Solutions has been carefully thought through – it makes it clear that it was made by a master craftsman.

The 2027 nuCamp TAB 360 Is the Perfect Teardrop Trailer, Now With a King Bed
11 photos
Photo: nuCamp RV
In an ideal world, we'd all have our cake and eat it. We don't live in an ideal world but, in many ways, this teardrop trailer from nuCamp RV does: the TAB 360, widely considered the perfect teardrop, is getting even "more perfect" for the 2027 model year.
The TAB 360 , or T@B 360 by its original name, is one of the most popular, multi-award winning, and compact trailers from U.S.-based manufacturer nuCamp RV. Introduced a couple of years ago as the perfect, three-season option for a single traveler or a couple of adventurers who still wanted some of the creature comforts of home on the road, it's been refreshed with almost every new iteration.
Not that it wasn't pretty neat to begin with. Shortly after its debut, it was named RV Pro's Best New Model for 2025 and RV News' RV of the Year, and went on to be universally (but unofficially) crowned "the perfect teardrop" in the following year.
You obviously can't improve perfection, but you can improve this teardrop – and nuCamp just did. For the 2027 model year, the TAB 360 gets the option of a king bed and more versatility in the back area, more standard features, and more functionality, without a spike in dry weight or its original dimensions.
Photo: nuCamp RV In simpler words, the TAB 360 is the same, but also better. The original layout remains virtually unchanged, but nuCamp tweaks and refines features, and further enhances the base package, now called Boondock, so that the interior space is cozier, packed with more everyday functionality, and nicer.
The TAB 360 still rides on a single pitched axle with electric brakes, alloy wheels, and offroad tires, and still comes in at 16.8 feet (5.1 meters) of overall length and 7.4 feet (2.2 meters) in width, offering full standing height inside. Dry weight is still at 2,605 lbs (1,181 kg), with 359 lbs (163 kg) of tongue weight and a gross weight of 3,900 lbs (1,769 kg).
The large aluminum box on the tongue is now standard, offering ample storage space and a separate compartment for one propane tank. This box is part of the optional Black Canyon package, and it's just one of the features that nuCamp implements in the standard Boondock base for the 2027 year, in what you could justly describe as a "more bang for your bucks" -type of situation.
Photo: nuCamp RV The layout still offers a front galley , a corner wet bathroom, and a rear living space split between a fixed bed and a two-person dinette that converts into another single bed. Even the storage options and the fact that overhead cabinets all come with soft-close hinges standard remain unchanged.
In previous years, this rear living arrangement offered sleeping in single beds, with the bonus for single travelers of having a fixed bed and a dining space, without the need to convert anything. For 2027, nuCamp adds the possibility to join the twins into a king bed, which makes the TAB 360 one of the few stand-in teardrops to boast a true king bed inside.
The transition is just as smooth as with converting the dinette and takes under one minute. Once the dinette drops down into a bed, you simply pull out two slatted extensions from the fixed bed, rearrange the cushions, and you have a full king. You do lose the nightstand between the two twins when you do that, but it's not like the storage space disappears; you'll still have it in the morning.
Photo: nuCamp RV Another big change to the 2027 TAB 360 is the galley kitchen, where nuCamp is trying to streamline it to offer a bit more working space. So, the previous two-burner cooktop and sink combo that took up the entire counter is being replaced with a much smaller single-burner and sink combo unit under a glass cover.
It seems that nuCamp believes customers would much rather cook outside or not at all on vacation, because this cooktop-sink unit looks too compact to be fully functional. You can definitely put together a quick breakfast on it, but not a proper meal. On the bright side, you still get a large 12V fridge with freezer, ample storage throughout, and the possibility to add a microwave in one of the cabinets over the fixed bed.
Also new for 2027 is composite flooring and tank heaters on all the holding tanks. The TAB 360 also has an enclosed underbelly, Alde underfloor radiant heat, and a Truma roof-mounted AC, which makes it a suitable option as an extended 3-season RV.
Photo: nuCamp RV Also part of the standard package for 2027 is the Nautilus water management system with an external shower, a 24-inch smart TV with Bluetooth stereo, reading lights, charging ports and power outlets, and a tiny wet bathroom that is surprisingly chic and practical.
It's the same one from previous years, with a 5-gallon (19-liter) bench cassette toilet, a tiny sink on top of it with a pull-out faucet, a porthole window, and a large mirror.
The TAB 360 also carries 25 gallons (95 liters) of freshwater and 18 gallons (68 liters) of gray, and it comes with stabilizers on all four corners, a full spare, dual-pane acrylic windows, red underbody lighting, two Stargazer windows that open, and a one-piece fiberglass roof with 380W of solar standard , hooked up to a 100Ah lithium battery that you can upgrade up to 270Ah with a 3000W inverter.
Photo: nuCamp RV "With its modern design, premium amenities, and high-quality craftsmanship, the TAB 360 offers an ideal blend of space and convenience," nuCamp says in the description for this tiny but packed travel trailer.
This kind of blend will set you back some $40,000-$50,000, depending on the dealer you work with and the options you add on top of the standard ones.

This Rendered GT Looks a Lot Better Than Anything Jaguar Currently Makes
16 photos
Photo: Instagram | alex_12_avo
Do you remember when Jaguar used to make nice cars? You likely do, as it hasn’t been that long since that happened.
However, this otherwise iconic British brand is now trying to reinvent itself and position further upmarket in an attempt to take a swing at Bentley and Rolls-Royce. And it has the Type 01 for that, an unconventional electric vehicle that does not care about anything the automaker once stood for.
Previewed by the Type 00 Concept, it was unveiled earlier this year, and does not look like any other road-legal Jaguar out there. There’s no traditional grille at the front, it features high shoulder lines, and if it weren’t for the panoramic roof, then the cockpit would have felt more like a tomb. There’s no rear window, and the cabin looks like it came from the space age.
The order books for the Jaguar 01 are expected to open in 2027, with the model expected to start at $130,000 in our market, and 130,000 pounds (equal to $171,190) in the UK. It features three electric motors for a total of 1,015 hp and 1,007 lb-ft (1,365 Nm) of torque, and it has an EPA range of 400 miles (644 km), according to Jag’, with its 118 kWh NMC battery pack fully charged.
Photo: Instagram | alex_12_avo Jaguar has clearly been criticized for attempting to reinvent itself, especially since the 01 does not look like anything it has even come from this company’s portfolio, and only time will tell if this was the right move. In the meantime, the rendering world, or a small chunk of it to be more precise, keeps imagining various Jaguar projects that will never see the light of day.
One of the latest to have crossed our screens can be seen in the gallery above. It has @alex_12_avo behind it, and was shared on social media earlier this week. The pixel-infused model is simply called the Jaguar GT , and to be honest, it definitely looks like an everyday grand tourer that one would expect to encounter at the golf course.
It features a very exotic overall design, with a vented hood, a pair of LED headlights, a large grille flanked by a pair of vents, an aggressive profile, muscular wheel arches, broad shoulders, and a back-end that looks more like an Aston Martin than a Jag’, this writer believes.
Nevertheless, that doesn’t make it any less exciting, and to be honest, this thing does indeed look a lot better than anything Jaguar currently makes, as mentioned in the title. And by that, we clearly mean the 01. So, if you had to choose between the quirky Jaguar 01 with its EV powertrain and this rendered GT that features ICE power, what color would the latter have? EICMA 2026 • Yamaha Births New Adventure Scooter Family, Three RW Models That Look More Like Motorcycles
Bentley Speed 16 Concept Virtually Entices Us to Imagine a V16 Competitor for the Bugatti Tourbillon
7 photos
Photo: zijie8783 / Instagram
The ultra-luxury British automaker Bentley is currently focused on launching their latest model – the brand’s first all-electric nameplate, Torcal, a crossover SUV packing up to 876 hp on a dedicated platform shared with the recent Porsche Cayenne Electric.
The new Bentley Torcal was launched in September 2026, sharing the Premium Platform Electric (PPE) created by the Volkswagen Group brands Audi and Porsche with the Cayenne Electric. Nothing will give away that relationship on the outside because the Torcal has a new design language that’s fresh even for Bentley, though inside the curved screen is a clear giveaway.
Anyway, less than two months since Bentley pulled the wraps off its first-ever production electric vehicle, the Torcal, and the model has already received a special commission. The Bentley x FRGMT Torcal is not a bespoke creation, with production capped at 20 units, and it’s made in collaboration with Hiroshi Fujiwara, “a pioneer of Tokyo’s Ura-Harajuku streetwear movement,” along with Mulliner, of course.
But not everyone is interested in EVs. Luckily, Bentley still offers the ICE and hybrid Bentayga, Continental GT, and Flying Spur models, allowing for ample choice as far as its exotic nature is concerned. The company will continue to produce internal combustion models as it recently backtracked from the EV-focused strategy it wanted to implement not long ago.
Of course, the parallel universes of vehicular CGI have quickly taken advantage of that, thanks to a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators. Zijie Yang, a virtual designer better known as ' zijie8783 ' on social media, is actually an Exterior Designer at XPeng, aka Guangzhou Xiaopeng Motors Technology, so we'd better listen to what his CGIs have to say about the automotive industry.
In his latest unofficial, hypothetical design project, the pixel master imagined a Bentley Speed 16 concept car, dubbed a ‘hyper GT’ model. It could easily be used by Bentley as a new model above the current Continental GT series or simply to influence the latter’s fifth generation when it’s time to change the current iteration around 2030. Also, the suggestion is to use a V16 powertrain!
Well, that’s not a bad idea – that way Bentley could become a little more than just a Rolls-Royce competitor. With Bugatti out of the Volkswagen AG stable after this year’s severance of the shares package, it wouldn’t be impossible to imagine that one of their brands needs to take on a more exotic role.
So, while Lamborghini takes care of the high-end supercar area, Bentley could easily slot into the previous grand tourer space occupied by Bugatti and create something like this with a massive V16 under the hood as a competitor for the Tourbillon hypercar. Cool or not? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Smart Yang (@zijie8783)

World's Most Expensive Mopar, a 1971 Hemi Cuda 4-Speed Ragtop, Shines at MCACN; $4.8M Was Not Enough
43 photos
Photo: Mecum (2021)
Ask any muscle car devotee to name the priciest Hemi Mopar in history, and most will cite the Bright Blue 1971 Plymouth Hemi Cuda convertible that hammered for $3.5 million at Mecum Seattle in 2014, topping $3.75 million with fees. Dismiss that benchmark as downright cheap. The true monarch is this other 1971 Hemi Cuda ragtop, the other E-body Plymouth 4-speed made that year, a unicorn so costly that nobody could afford it at Mecum Indy 2021 despite a $4.8 million high bid. Of course, that didn’t stop it from making a guest star appearance at the ongoing Muscle Car and Corvette Nationals.
When bidding stalled at $4.8 million in Indianapolis with the reserve still firmly unmet—well shy of its $5.75 million to $6.5 million pre-sale estimate—the collector world witnessed automotive royalty flex its untouchable status. Recently, aul Grasso, the YouTuber from Grasso’s Garage, spotted this exact Winchester Gray legend sitting casually on the show floor in Rosemont, Illinois, for the 2026 edition of the greatest muscle car and Corvette show on Planet Piston.
The majestic Hemicuda is still wearing its vintage French license plate, 423 HD 19, and commanding silent reverence from everyone passing by. Even the YouTuber, a seasoned enthusiast who has owned a 1970 Cuda for 35 years, standing beside this drop-top felt surreal. Among the dozen Hemi ‘Cuda convertibles Plymouth built for 1971, it stands alone as the sole example painted in Winchester Gray metallic.
Dressed with a black soft top, matte black Hemi billboard graphics, a black Shaker scoop, body-color mirrors, and Rallye wheels wrapped in Goodyear Polyglas GT rubber, it looks devastatingly poised.
Step beside the cabin and the specification grows even more intoxicating. Black vinyl high-back bucket seats frame power windows, a woodgrain center console, matching dash accents, a three-spoke sport steering wheel, and the iconic Hurst Pistol Grip shifter. Peer into the Rallye gauge cluster and you spot its rarest quirk: a factory export metric speedometer calibrated to 240 kph, an Old World touch that elevates this Detroit bruiser into genuinely 1-of-1 territory.
Photo: Mecum (2021) Beneath that Shaker scoop rests its original, numbers-matching 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi V8, breathing through the signature twin fours (dual four-barrel) carburetors. Rated at 425 horsepower and 490 lb-ft of torque (431 PS, 664 Nm), this must have felt like a locomotive over on French roads. Behind the Elephant sits the original New Process A833 4-speed manual.
Equipped with power steering, power brakes, and the A33 Track Pak, the ‘Cuda puts power down through a Dana 60 Sure Grip rear axle with 3.54 gears. The big-block behemoth needed a 26-inch radiator and seven-blade viscous fan to keep it from steaming itself to death under wide-open throttle applications.
I’m not sure French motorists were into quarter-mile drag racing back in the seventies, though, so this surreal pony car might have actually lived a quiet, serene life, unlike many of its close or distant siblings from the Detroit side of the Atlantic.
Photo: Mecum (2021) Its provenance reads like a collector's fever dream. Built at Hamtramck as an export order, this Cuda shipped new to France, where enthusiast Jean Teyssier acquired it and savored it across European roads for more than 20 years, logging roughly 90,000 kilometers (some 58k miles). In 1993, an American buyer answered a shockingly modest U.S. car club newsletter listing simply advertising a 1971 gray Cuda, flew straight to France, and triumphantly repatriated this transatlantic treasure.
Roughly six years after returning home, the car entered the stewardship of collector Tom Lembeck, who safeguarded it for over 20 years in preserved, numbers-matching condition . Rather than erasing its soul through over-restoration, he kept its original broadcast sheet, original French title, and import documents intact.
Crossing the Mecum Indy stage in May 2021, its metric odometer displayed 98,553 kilometers, or 61,238 miles, proving this thoroughbred was genuinely driven, cherished, and respected.
Photo: Mecum (2021) Understanding why collectors worship this car requires revisiting the brief, incandescent life of the Hemi Cuda itself. Styled for 1970 by John E. Herlitz on Chrysler's wider, shorter E-body platform, the third-generation Barracuda finally boasted an engine bay cavernous enough for the NASCAR-bred 426 Hemi.
Yet steep $4,000 sticker prices, punishing insurance surcharges, and looming emissions rules restricted the Hemi Cuda to just two glorious model years, 1970 and 1971. From the start, the roofless Hemi Cuda stood as an engineering triumph and a showroom unicorn, with extra unibody reinforcement driving prices even higher.
In 1970, out of 48,867 Barracudas built, ChryCo delivered 666 U.S.-market Hemi Cudas: 652 hardtops and just 14 domestic convertibles, divided into five with the 4-speed manual and nine with the TorqueFlite automatic. Factoring in three Canadian deliveries and one overseas export brought total 1970 Hemi Cuda convertible output to just 18 cars.
Photo: YouTube/ Grassos Garage (@grassosgarage2248) For 1971, Plymouth added quad headlights, fender gills, and billboard graphics for the Hemi's swansong, yet market headwinds decimated volume. Total Barracuda production tumbled to 16,492 units, leaving just 114 U.S.-market Hemi Cudas: 107 hardtops and seven domestic convertibles, split into two with the 4-speed manual and five automatics. Counting export orders lifted global 1971 convertible totals to 12 units—merely three with the 4-speed manual and nine with the TorqueFlite automatic.
Stack those numbers against Mopar's broader legacy and the rarity turns staggering. Across 1970 and 1971 combined, Plymouth built just 780 US-spec Hemi Cudas, making the 21 domestic convertibles (out of a global production of 30) a microscopic elite.
Widen the scope across Chrysler's entire 1966 to 1971 Hemi run spanning every Dodge and Plymouth model, totaling 10,904 cars (9,761 Street Hemis), and the trio of 1971 4-speed convertibles represent barely 0.03 percent of all Street Hemi Mopars ever produced.
Photo: YouTube/ Grassos Garage (@grassosgarage2248) Unsurprisingly, these open-air icons rewrote collector economics. A Hemi Cuda convertible became the first muscle car to breach $1 million at auction in 2002. A Tor-Red 1971 automatic reached $2.2 million at Barrett-Jackson in 2007, and another fetched $2.25 million at Mecum Monterey in 2015. At Mecum Kissimmee 2016, a 1970 4-speed brought $2.675 million while the first-built 1971 automatic hit $2.3 million, before soaring to $3.3 million at Kissimmee in January 2026.
Yet every one of those landmark sales lives in the shadow of this Winchester Gray French export. With its numbers-matching 426 Hemi, Pistol Grip 4-speed, metric gauges, unassailable transatlantic provenance, and singular factory finish, it stands above every winged warrior and domestic convertible ever hammered.
Turning down $4.8 million was not stubbornness; it was recognition that some automotive monuments transcend price tags altogether, forever crowning this 1971 Hemi Cuda convertible as the undisputed Holy Grail of American muscle.

Dodge Hellcat Redeye Challenges Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 to a Drag Race, It's Over in 10 Seconds
8 photos
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Wheels
Discontinued muscle cars are not dead, and if you doubt that, then you have likely forgotten about the fact that the Chevrolet Camaro is dead, and that the modern-day Dodge Charger is not (yet) available with a V8.
This means that the S650 Ford Mustang is the only model within this game to still be offered with an eight-cylinder unit under the hood. The offer is quite vast, when it comes to these models, as you get not only the regular GT with a 5.0-liter naturally aspirated unit, but also the Dark Horse. These are joined by the insane Dark Horse SC, with its 795 hp, and the 815-hp Mustang GTD, set to be joined soon by the even crazier GTD Competition.
Mind you, we haven’t gathered here today to discuss the new-age muscle car kingdom, but to put the spotlight on a drag racing video. Shared at the bottom of the page, the footage is a little over one minute long. It was shot at the Las Vegas Speedway presumably not long ago, and shows a quarter-mile brawl between a Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat Redeye Widebody and an S550 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500, which was over in 10 seconds.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Wheels As you likely remember, the Hellcat versions of the discontinued Dodge Challenger were offered with a little over 700 horsepower in their most basic versions. The superior ones, which featured an uprated version of the same 6.2-liter supercharged V8, had more than 800 horsepower to play with, and these were veritable 10-second machines, taking in the region of 3.5 seconds to sprint to 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill. And they are still capable of impressive performance when it comes to straight-line duels.
The S550-based Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 was (and still is) a formidable opponent to the Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat family. It also needs in the region of three and a half seconds to reach 60 mph from zero, and it is a 10-second car on a good day, with a skilled driver behind the wheel. Its 5.2-liter supercharged V8 engine produces 760 horsepower with zero outside intervention, and that is something to write home about even by today’s standards.
But how do these two models compare in a head-to-head battle down the quarter mile from a standing start? Well, you have likely witnessed such fights several times over the years, and it is now time to put the spotlight on one of the latest. As we already told you, it was all over in 10 seconds, and the two were separated by pretty much a hair when they crossed the finish line. Can you spot the winner? Now head on down and watch the short video to see if you were right.

Move Over 'James Bondisson' and GTA VI Because Lamborghini Rocked LA With the Temerario Spyder
14 photos
Photo: Lamborghini
This has been a very interesting week, and the ongoing 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show is the culmination of things for automotive fans – the ones that don’t feel sad or enraged about Robert Pattinson being cast by Amazon MGM Studios as the next James Bond and the ones that aren’t too tired after playing non-stop GTA VI since it launched, that is.
I kind of fell out of bed on Monday morning when I heard that none of the final-five actors that were in the books to play the next James Bond actually got the part, and Amazon MGM Studios went with the ‘safe’ casting of Twilight-saga star Robert Pattinson. There’s a lot to talk about the Hollywood star, who has worked hard to get rid of the shiny vampire banter over his formative years.
Some will like this idea; others will not. I have mixed feelings – I would have loved to see a relatively unknown actor take over the mantle and make James Bond their own just like Daniel Craig, Pierce Brosnan, or the late and beloved Sean Connery did in their times. I think that it’s a Disney move to play it safe with someone who already has a ton of work behind their back.
There’s also the situation with The Batman – this guy may be a cool and modern Hollywood star, but he’s not immortal (pun intended) and doesn’t have time to commit to a couple of massive franchises at the same time. However, there is one major glimmer of hope – the next 007 installment is being directed by Denis Villeneuve, which I think is one of those directors like Christopher Nolan who can live up to the standards of blockbusters imposed by Steven Spielberg and James Cameron.
Photo: Amazon MGM Also, we can already make fun of the casting – the viral portmanteau nickname for Robert Pattinson and his new Amazon MGM role is “James Bondisson,” created in line with Barbenheimer or the upcoming Dunesday. Now, let’s talk about the big elephant in the PlayStation and Xbox realm – Grand Theft Auto VI . By the way, I have a confession to make.
Although I loved playing games when I was in my prime – those years when girls and cars were the only things that mattered (along with planes, at least for me) – the GTA franchise never spoke to my heart, as I would rather play Call of Duty or Diablo or even NFS instead. But my adolescent kid has taken a liking to GTA V, so of course I’m in touch with the 13-year wait for the sixth installment.
The new game came out this week precisely when 007 is also new, and Anthropic has also gone for IPO greatness on top of everything – just to also touch on the hot subject of AI and avoid any Nvidia and its ousted CEO discussions. So, for me, GTA VI hasn’t been a major interest – though I did stay in touch, especially poking fun with my boy (who is patiently waiting for the game as a gift sometime down the line) about folks taking a week off from work and even signing agreements with their spouses and kids to make sure they’re not disturbed.
Photo: Rockstar Games One thing I did keep a closer eye on was the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show , which used to be a major draw for automakers because it’s the final hurrah of the automotive season ahead of the Christmas holidays. Unfortunately, either because of a confluence of factors or due to the James Bondisson, Anthropic IPO, and especially the GTA VI off time of employees, this year’s Automobility LA and the LA Auto Show itself have been rather bland and uninteresting.
That’s not to say there weren’t any cool premieres, like the Rivian R2, the eighth generation of the Hyundai Elantra, the 2027 Chrysler Pacifica Copperline, and a bunch of other minor novelties from the likes of Acura and Honda all the way up to Volkswagen. In fact, I think the Elantra deserves a ton of appreciation because Hyundai continues to cater to the affordable compact sedan space.
Photo: Lamborghini However, the coolest automobile this week is the new Lamborghini Temerario Spyder launched on the eve of the 2026 LA Auto Show both in Sant’Agata Bolognese and Los Angeles. Well, if you asked me about the coupe before this release, I would have said the Huracan successor is a nice technical tour de force but also a little bland, especially when seen from the front because the rear can’t make any mistakes when you’re mid-engined and packing 907 hp.
But somehow, without changing the front, which remains boring, the rear is a festival of coolness thanks to that crazy vertical-stowing hardtop roof that not only makes the Temerario look like a real Spyder, as if there’s no roof whatsoever, but also enhances handling because of a lower center of gravity when the car is roofless. Now I really hope the Revuelto Roadster goes down the same route… View this post on Instagram A post shared by James Bond 007 (@007) View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rockstar Games (@rockstargames)

Waze Starts Showing Raised Crossing Notifications on Android Auto and CarPlay
8 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
Waze has started showing notifications for incoming raised crossings, therefore giving drivers more time to slow down.
While the ability to add raised crossings to Waze has been around since at least July for map editors, the notifications have now started to appear for drivers in Europe. Considering these are considered permanent road features, which map editors must manually add to the map based on their location, users won’t be able to report them through the hazard reporting button.
If the raised crossings don’t show up for you just yet, the best option is to reach out to your local Waze map editor community and wait for the maps to be updated.
Prior to this update, the raised crossings were marked on the map as a speed bump. The introduction of this update makes more sense, as the raised crossings also allow pedestrians to cross the street and also double as a speed bump.
The introduction of raised crossing notifications is not tied to a specific app version, as the alerts are pushed through a server-side update. However, you should still update to the latest version to get the most recent bug fixes and improvements. I am using the most recent Waze version published on the App Store on an iPhone 15 Pro and CarPlay, but the raised crossings also appear on my wife’s iPhone 17 that runs an older version of Waze.
Meanwhile, the addition of this feature also serves as another reminder that Google still doesn’t plan to merge Google Maps and Waze. The reason is as simple as it can be: while Google Maps remains an all-in-one mapping platform that focuses on the essential capabilities and only gets the common traffic hazards, Waze keeps expanding into new directions with support for more traffic reports.
For example, while Waze can warn of speed bumps and raised crossings, Google Maps only shows user-reported hazards, such as accidents and roadworks. Google Maps also imports police reports from Waze, but otherwise, the application doesn’t support permanent road features similar to those currently available in Waze.
The raised crossing alerts are live on all platforms where Waze is available, including not only mobile devices, but also Android Auto and CarPlay. This makes sense, considering the experience on Android Auto and CarPlay is still powered by a smartphone. You’ll see an alert on the screen when you approach a pinned raised crossing - you can also disable these notifications separately, as they are part of the permanent road features group.
If you want to disable all permanent road features in Waze, including raised crossings and speed bumps, you must open the app, tap the icon to open the side menu, and head over to Settings > Map Display > Reports, and look for the one that you want to block from showing up on the screen.

GTA 6 Will Certainly Want To Check Out This 1970 Ford, Only One Ever Made
32 photos
Photo: eBay seller txchopper67
A 1970 Ford Ranchero is selling at auction on eBay, and if you’ve played GTA 6 , you have every reason to be excited about this pickup truck. The reason is as simple as it could be: this is the first car protagonist Jason owns in GTA 6, albeit under a different name for obvious licensing reasons.
The Vapid Ganado is Jason’s original ride, and as I told you a few days ago, it’s based on the 1970 Ranchero in almost every regard .
This Ranchero is more than just a source of inspiration for Rockstar. The owner claims it’s the only one ever made in this configuration, and they also included the Marti report to prove it.
Photo: eBay seller txchopper67 The Ranchero lineup for 1970 included the standard model, the 500, the GT, and the Squire.
Buyers who were specifically interested in a luxurious pickup truck were recommended to order the Squire. Described as “the new ultimate in personal pickup luxury,” the Ranchero Squire sported a contoured woodtone side and tailgate panels, plush full-width seats, wall-to-wall carpeting, a woodtone panel under the instruments, and an electric clock.
Ford also offered a long list of options, such as the Rim-Blow sport steering wheel, the SelectShift Cruise-O-Matic transmission, an AM/FM stereo radio, hidden headlamps, and the famous SelectAire conditioner.
As for the engine lineup, the Ranchero series included a little something for everybody, beginning with a 250 six rated at 155 horsepower. The Squire received unrestricted access to the most powerful engines in the lineup, so if money wasn’t an issue, you could even order one of the two 429 engines.
The Thunder Jet produced 360 horsepower thanks to a four-barrel carburetor and a 10.5:1 compression ratio, while the Cobra benefited from a higher compression ratio - 11.3:1 - to produce no more, no less than 370 horsepower.
Photo: eBay seller txchopper67 This Ranchero isn’t necessarily as special as a 429-powered specimen, at least not from an engine perspective. It is fitted with a 302 and an automatic transmission, but the original owner also ordered several desirable options, including air conditioning.
The 302 engine is now fully functional, but worth knowing is that this Ranchero has already received a tune-up, so it’s almost in perfect shape. It’s unclear if the engine was rebuilt, but the 302 was added to the list of items that were repaired recently, so I would call the seller and ask for more details on this front.
The clock in the dash is no longer functional, and the cruise control system also requires some attention. You can tell this isn’t a spotless car by simply looking at it, as it suffers from surface rust and blemishes that require some attention if your objective is a specimen in tip-top shape to park in your collection.
You get the obvious package, including power steering and power brakes, and the owner says the truck will come with a new hard cover and a new vinyl side and rear graphics.
The air conditioning blows cold but needs an in-depth verification because it’s still not running completely correctly.
Photo: eBay seller txchopper67 Now, let’s get to the thing that makes this Ranchero truly special. The Marti report that the owner has already ordered for this Ranchero Squire reveals impressive numbers, and there’s a good chance that this is the number one selling point.
Out of all 3,943 Rancher Squires produced for this model year, only 1,099 were fitted with a 302 V8 engine under the hood. This is already a low number, but the report doesn’t stop here. It’s getting a lot more interesting, as only 74 of all these trucks were painted Light Gold. Only 54 people ordered the Nugget Gold knitted vinyl bench seats, and - this is the part where the numbers are getting truly impressive - only 3 were equipped with evaporative emissions.
Two of these Rancheros got the Visibility Light Group, and just one - this one! - came with air conditioning.
If these numbers don’t convince you to buy this Ranchero, I don’t know what will, so this is now the right moment to talk money.
Photo: eBay seller txchopper67 The vehicle is selling at auction, but the bad news is that a reserve is also in place. With only 9 hours remaining until the auction comes to an end, the reserve is still in place, so there’s a good chance the Ranchero will remain where it is for a little longer.
The pickup truck could find a new home at the very last minute, if one of the 190 people who added it to their watchlists decide to submit an offer that can unlock the reserve. The top offer at the time of writing is $7,271, and I expect the reserve to be somewhere around $10K.
The vehicle is parked in El Paso, Texas, and it should be able to go anywhere on its wheels, considering its fantastic shape.

Oversized and No-Wood DXL Teardrop Camper Can Be Transformed Into an Off-Grid Family-Ready Campsite
10 photos
Photo: RD Trailers
Travel trailers are one of the fastest ways to head into the wild and over the years, there have been countless styles that have popped up, some even enduring the test of time. However, in all the hubbub, there’s one style that managed to be called upon year after year. That design is the teardrop camper.
We all know a teardrop camper when we see one, and because these RVs are some of the most compact around, can be filled with only the essentials we require, and are even able to sometimes be used well through all four seasons of the year, it makes them one of the most called-upon designs on our roads.
Even variations of the traditional teardrop camper exist, one of the most common being the squaredrop, classic designs without the tapered of rear end and a blockier look and design. It’s often produced by brands that also craft units in the vintage style.
Photo: RD Trailers One such team is RD Trailers (RDT), an American crew born in the heart of camper and RV mecca: Indiana. But, unlike other big-name brands out there, RDT doesn’t belong to some conglomerate, but operates on their own, inviting future camper owners to work closely with the hands that actually put their dream machines together.
It’s here that we find the Transformer DXL, a camper that taps into the timeless teardrop design to grant us access to a lifestyle where we can take in breaths of unpolluted air, sleep without sirens and cars honking in the background, and wake with a view to the view of the sun rising over the horizon.
One little difference that needs to be considered regarding the DXL is that the rear of the body is a bit more rounded than the “teardrop” shape that the traditional design calls upon, and there’s a reason for it: space.
Photo: RD Trailers As a result, the overall length of the DXL comes in at 190 inches long, with the cabin itself occupying 124 of those inches (10.3 ft) in length. Oh, and in classic fashion, RT still places the kitchen at the rear, accessible by a hatch that we lift overhead and even use as an awning during light rains and to keep debris from falling into your pan while cooking.
The galley is also where we see a bit about how RDT builds these campers. Take a close look at the racks, slideouts, and cabinet too; they’re built from good old aluminum, leaving out a material that is typically called upon in teardrop camper construction: wood. One exception to the all-aluminum build is the countertop which is constructed out of steel.
Come to think of it, the entire DXL is crafted without wood, not a single drop. The walls and roof are primarily built from this alloy, the framing, and everything else to. The result is a glamping solution that weighs under 1,700 lbs (772 kg) dry with standard features.
Photo: RD Trailers Wildly enough, RD states that with all add-on options they have in store for future DXL owners, the unit still weighs under 2,000 lbs (907 kg). The thing is that you won’t need much to call upon. I mean, included in the $20,665 (€18,800) price tag that RD has stamped on a standard unit, we do receive a Delta 2 battery bank from EcoFlow, and all we need is a solar panel or two and that’s that.
If you’re worried about weight limits, don’t be since the camper can take a full 3,000 lbs (1,360 kg) of load. But, you shouldn’t be loading you’re rig up to the max if you plan on riding around off-road. With an underslung fresh water tank, 14 inches of ground clearance is available to play with out there but consider that a torsion axle is in place as standard and AT tires on 15-inch rims ensure you can breakaway from tarmac and onto rougher roads.
What we also need to consider in terms of abilities is that we can expand this camper into a family-ready one. All we need is to drop a roof-top tent on the DXL and then load it up with all the goods and requisites that you need out there. Don’t forget to bring ample water.
Photo: RD Trailers That roof rack is also suitable for things like kayaks, as we can see in the image gallery, awnings, and at the front, on top of the storage box on the nose cone, more space, and even the ability to add a bike rack. I mean, what more could you want from a lightweight and compact camper?
What I do recommend is a heating system. That way, you can extend your glamping season beyond the warmer months. Don’t forget an AC for the mid-day heat. Parking it in the shade is also a great way to reduce your dependency on cooling and actually help your exterior coat stay intact for longer. Don’t forget camper upkeep; I digress.
That said, the DXL isn’t the first teardrop camper, nor the last, but it does have a place in the heart of some Americans that may be seeking a lightweight and properly built modern teardrop camper. Until next time.

source_document.body:
For decades, Briggs & Stratton has helped keep the lights on after the storm with its gas-powered generators. Now, the company is bringing that legacy to the electric age with a new 16 kWh backup battery designed to scale with your growing energy needs.
Briggs & Stratton partnered with Texas-based EG4 to offer an all American-branded solution for battery backup power solution last year , and its stackable SimpliPHI batteries helped make it easy to right-size home battery projects – but those batteries were limited in size , and limited in what they could actually offer. With the launch of the brand’s new, 16 kWh SimpliPHI battery, the company is ready to meet your energy needs … even if those needs take you up to 512 kWh. (!)
For context, the average US home uses about 865 kWh of energy per month , so a 512 kWh battery should theoretically keep your lights on for nearly 18 days after a storm – or provide basic power for your whole block for a weekend, at least!
“This launch represents a significant shift in our battery strategy,” explains Sequoya Cross, vice president of energy storage at Briggs & Stratton. “Our combined resources allow us to bring a competitively priced battery of the highest quality to energy storage installers.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
An onboard battery management system (BMS) and built-in Wi-Fi gateway help to streamline the system’s setup for installers, while the Briggs battery’s automatic inverter sensing technology supports closed-loop communication with Sol-Ark, Solis , EG4, Growatt, Megarevo, Victron, and other leading inverters. Other installer-friendly features include an IP65-rated enclosure allows for indoor or outdoor installation in either ground- or wall-mounted setups without requiring an additional cabinet, and an integrated circuit breaker that allows technicians to isolate the battery during servicing.
The battery itself is rated for 8,000 cycles at 90% depth of discharge, with a charge and discharge rate of 0.5C and an end-of-life capacity of 70%. Briggs & Stratton backs its new battery packs with a 12-year parts warranty that includes labor and travel costs, as well as a US-based tech support service.
The SimpliPHI 16 is available for pre-order now, though pricing was not mentioned in the original press release .
